summary: Harness budget rails: per-run cap (turns floor always-measurable + optional tokens ceiling), hard stop -> blocked:budget receipt, ledger-as-receipt every run, execution seam as a lookup table. Survey-first (built only the gap), additive orchestrator wiring, proven with two run artifacts + an end-to-end orchestrator halt, 26 pytest, and six adversarial verifiers all HOLDS.

findings.claim: Survey (Target 1): five existing meters are each scope-distinct from a per-run spend cap. token_ceiling.json = STATIC preload budget of the tool catalog, and its claimed enforcer checks.py::check_tool_surface_deferred DOES NOT EXIST (grep-clean) - it is enforced by nothing.

The source of truth for MEASURED tokens is the transcript JSONL message.usage.{input_tokens,output_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens}, read by NO existing script. econ_transcript_cost.py substitutes a chars/3.6 PROXY - the exact estimate a ledger must not use. rails.py reads the real usage; when absent it renders UNKNOWN, never an estimate.

memory STATE spawn_ledger caps AGENT-TURNS via a fail-closed capCheck (the pattern rails mirrors), but its subagent_tokens field is hand-transcribed on one entry and enforced by nothing. .synapse/harness.py --budget tracks USD but writes no receipt and always exits 0, so a budget block is not signalled as a failure. rails.py supplies the missing receipt + non-zero exit + hard stop.

Adversarial verification (6 skeptics) confirmed all four crucible criteria and both invariants HOLD: no estimate reaches a ledger field; the hard stop is real and not trivially always-on; orchestrate.ps1 is byte-for-byte additive; the seam is a pure lookup with no dispatch primitive; a tokens-only cap is refused and the turns floor bites even under a ~1e9 token ceiling with an UNKNOWN meter (never unlimited); a missing transcript yields UNKNOWN, not 0.
